steps.name: Fit interaction model and test condition:time coefficients
caveats: Length offset lost: the salmon gene table carries no length information, so a change in isoform use can show as differential expression; state this in the report (R-0169@18ab).

Interaction power is low at 3 replicates per cell: the interaction coefficient is a difference of two differences with a larger standard error than a main effect. Keep the interaction test primary, report simple effects beside it (T1S3), state the power limit in the report, and do not loosen the threshold (R-0063@6190, R-0162@ed74, R-0017@8a47).
With 3 replicates per cell DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cook's distance and sets p to NA; report those genes separately from independent-filtering NAs (R-0039@968d).
No batch column exists in the metadata; if the T1S1 PCA shows structure that condition and time do not explain, report it as a limitation rather than adding an unidentifiable batch term.
steps.context: counts.csv is a gene-level table from salmon with no per-sample quantification files and no average-transcript-length table, so the import state is unestablished and the model fits the counts as delivered with no length offset. time is a 4-level factor with t0 as reference; the interaction spans 3 coefficients, one per post-t0 time level.

plan.title: Treatment-by-time interaction DE in human cell line
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is an interaction question: which genes change differently over time under treatment than under control, i.e. a condition x time effect beyond the shared time trend. The data are gene-level counts (12000 genes x 24 samples, salmon-derived) with a 2 condition x 4 time point (t0..t3) design, 3 replicates per cell. The plan fits a single DESeq2 model with ~ condition + time + condition:time, tests the condition:time coefficients with the Wald test (each coefficient is one time level versus the reference t0, with apeglm shrinkage and BH within contrast), and reports the simple effects - the treatment effect at each time point - beside the interaction contrasts with ashr shrinkage for non-coefficient contrasts. Blind VST PCA and sample-distance QC run before the model because no batch column exists in the metadata; any structure that does not follow condition or time must be seen before testing. Known limits carried into the report: the counts are a salmon gene table with no length data, so the model fits the counts as delivered with no length offset (an isoform-usage change can surface as DE), and with 3 replicates per cell the interaction contrast - a difference of differences - has low power, so thresholds stay at the defaults and the power limit is stated rather than compensated.

No batch column exists in the metadata; if the T1S1 PCA shows structure that condition and time do not explain, report it as a limitation rather than adding an unidentifiable batch term.

plan.title: Treatment-by-time interaction DE in human cell line
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is an interaction question: which genes change differently over time under treatment than under control, i.e. a condition x time effect beyond the shared time trend. The data are gene-level counts (12000 genes x 24 samples, salmon-derived) with a 2 condition x 4 time point (t0..t3) design, 3 replicates per cell. The plan fits a single DESeq2 model with ~ condition + time + condition:time, tests the condition:time coefficients with the Wald test (each coefficient is one time level versus the reference t0, with apeglm shrinkage and BH within contrast), and reports the simple effects - the treatment effect at each time point - beside the interaction contrasts with ashr shrinkage for non-coefficient contrasts. Blind VST PCA and sample-distance QC run before the model because no batch column exists in the metadata; any structure that does not follow condition or time must be seen before testing. Known limits carried into the report: the counts are a salmon gene table with no length data, so the model fits the counts as delivered with no length offset (an isoform-usage change can surface as DE), and with 3 replicates per cell the interaction contrast - a difference of differences - has low power, so thresholds stay at the defaults and the power limit is stated rather than compensated.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

With two or three replicates per group, the design step states the expected power of the test before the model. The tools of record for a power and sample size calculation, RNASeqPower and PROPER, are not in the pool here. Compute the power from the closed form of the sample size in terms of the depth, the biological coefficient of variation, the fold change, and the significance level, or take the dispersion from a pilot or a public dataset of the same tissue, and state the fold change that the design can find with 80 percent power. State that a larger replicate count raises the power more than a deeper sequencing does. The statement is a caution on the plan and not a reason to loosen the threshold.

With an interaction question and three or fewer replicates in a cell of the design, the interaction term has low power. The interaction coefficient is a difference of two differences, thus its standard error is larger than the standard error of a main effect at the same replicate number. Keep the interaction test as the primary result, but report the simple effects in each level beside it, with the same threshold. State the power limit in the report, and do not loosen the threshold to compensate. A gene that is absent from the interaction list is not shown to have the same effect in both levels.

If the smallest group holds three replicates, the test has low power. Both count models find only a small share of the true differentially expressed genes, most of them with a large fold change. Interpret the result with caution, and state the power limit in the report. Keep alpha at its default value, and do not change the threshold to compensate for the small design. A gene that is not in the list is not shown to be unchanged.
